sentence: This project studies how a part of the brain called the striatum is involved in using fentanyl and methamphetamine together, using rats.
This project locates gene regions in cross progeny and uses CRISPR gene editing to find which genes in each region are causative.
This project surveys the human antibody response to human astrovirus infection and uses it to design and test a vaccine.
This project provides sequencing and analysis tools to study the transcriptome and epigenome of human hematopoietic stem cells.
This project focuses on cell signaling, epigenetics and genome maintenance, processes that are deregulated in cancer and aging.
This project works to ease the burden of cancer on patients and families through scientific collaboration and communication with communities.
This project builds data pipelines and analysis tools to study how the exposome affects health and community well-being.
This project offers genomics tools such as single-cell sequencing and spatial transcriptomics to support cancer research.
This project tests a smartphone program that teaches daily skills for building positive emotions to help adults with fibromyalgia reduce pain.
This project builds research tools that identify and measure biological macromolecules.
This project gives biostatistics and bioinformatics support to cancer research projects, from design to analysis.
This project coordinates the sharing of biospecimens and data among research collaborators.
This project develops a cold-responsive cancer therapy that targets tumor cells to treat both primary and metastatic cancer.
This project studies how glycine receptors and gephyrin form clusters at synapses and what those clusters do.
This project examines how aging biomarkers, DNA methylation and gene expression relate to each other, the environment and health over the life course.
This project tests whether functional near-infrared spectroscopy can reliably measure language-related brain activity in people with aphasia after stroke.
This project studies how selenium is absorbed, how it moves through the body and how it is used to build protective proteins.
This project develops chemical reagents to image formaldehyde in living systems and find where it comes from and what it acts on.
This project tries to find out how polycomb group proteins silence fetal hemoglobin in sickle cell disease and beta thalassemia.
This project uses natural language processing to find how clinician preconceptions about cannabis use show up in clinical documentation and shape prenatal care.
